blocks.name: quantized-checkpoint
blocks.reason: decode ran at 73% of the memory-bandwidth ceiling at the measured batch; a pre-quantized copy of this model runs on this GPU (compute capability 8.9). 8-bit: int8 W8A8, fp8 (W8A8). 4-bit, where answers change more often: AWQ int4, GPTQ int4, W4A16. int8 W8A8 and fp8 also run prompt processing in 8-bit arithmetic here

blocks.costs: TPOT rises when answers do not copy the prompt, and at high concurrency; a slower start
blocks.name: ngram-speculation
blocks.reason: prompts are long (median 494 words beyond what they share). N-gram speculation drafts tokens by copying spans of the prompt, so it only helps when answers quote or repeat their input; otherwise it costs a little - compare TPOT with and without it. Replaying prompt lookup on this run's answers, drafts would supply 17.4% of all output tokens, and 8.6% is needed to pay for the 4.5 ms each step adds (measured on an A10G at 32 running requests; this run's step is 48 ms)
blocks.test: about 11 min on this setup (this run: 257 s to load, 6.7 min to warm up and measure)

blocks.costs: the weights are quantized at every start; below compute capability 8.9 (T4, A10G) only the stored weights shrink, so prompt processing is no faster
blocks.name: fp8-weights
blocks.reason: decode ran at 73% of the memory-bandwidth ceiling at the measured batch; vLLM can store the weights in 8-bit fp8 when it starts, so each decode step reads half the weight bytes and the freed memory holds more requests (on this GPU the maths runs in 8 bits too)
blocks.test: about 11 min on this setup (this run: 257 s to load, 6.7 min to warm up and measure)

blocks.costs: TPOT p95 rises as larger chunks stall running decodes
blocks.name: raise-prefill-batch
blocks.reason: TTFT p50 is 17x TPOT p50 with requests waiting; the gate is 20x. Larger prefill chunks usually cut TTFT but can stall running decodes (TPOT p95) - measure both
blocks.test: about 11 min on this setup (this run: 257 s to load, 6.7 min to warm up and measure)
